title: Euler's totient is a finite-set cardinality
statement: The number of elements of the finite set {k < n : gcd k n = 1} equals totient n. The ad hoc bounded count that DEFINES the totient is a cardinality of a computed finite set.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Finset.card_totatives : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.Finset.card (AxNat.Finset.filter (fun (x1 : AxNat) => AxNat.beq (AxNat.gcd x1 x0) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (AxNat.Finset.range x0))) (AxNat.totient x0))

evidence.supports: Nat.Finset.card_totatives is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- Nat.Finset.card_totatives 2>/dev/null | grep -Fc '(AxNat.Finset.range x0))) (AxNat.totient x0)')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pattern is a DISTINGUISHING substring of the admitted type, not the theorem's name: an existence check would still pass if the statement drifted. Verified to fail on a perturbed pattern before this row was written. `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted kernel gate, so a successful build IS the type-check.

evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example theorem_axiom_footprint -- Finset 2>/dev/null | awk -F'\t' '$1 == "nat" && $2 == "Nat.Finset.card_totatives" && $3 == "0"' | wc -l)" -ge 1

The pattern pins BOTH the declaration name and the size 0 with an empty axiom column, so a proof that reached for a trusted declaration would fail the check rather than be reported as axiom-free. The `nat` prelude's whole trusted surface is empty, which bounds this independently.

evidence.supports: The definitions this statement is about COMPUTE the intended values, with negative controls -- the kernel cannot tell a Definition is wrong
evidence.notes: `Nat.Finset`'s operations are admitted on their TYPE; a `card` that computed the wrong number would have the right type, an empty axiom footprint, and would pass every other check in this ledger. `finset_tests.rs` reduces each operation to a numeral or a Bool at tiny discriminating arguments and pairs every positive with the specific wrong formula its negative control rules out. It caught one wrong hand-computed expectation while being written.

provenance.source: theorem name and canonical type read directly via nat_theorem_inventory, which prints render_lean of the admitted type; declared by `nat_prelude/finset.rs` (lane finset-role, ADR-1577).

notes: `Nat.totient` is DEFINED as `countRange (fun k => beq (gcd k n) 1) n` and `nat_prelude/totient.rs`'s own module doc reads that as |{k < n : p k}|. This makes the reading a theorem, with `Nat.totient` and every theorem already proved about it UNCHANGED. It is the consumer ADR-1577 records: a survey found NO site in nat_prelude/int_prelude where substituting the carrier shortens an existing proof, because the predicate-level algebra (nat_prelude/finite_set.rs) already exists; what was missing was an OBJECT, not a shorter proof. Any future totient argument may now be a set argument and reach `Nat.totient` through this one equation.
